        "Full28-file owned mixed local/vendor Rust diff read, including all changed inline test sections. The functional vendor update is included, not excluded as generated/imported bulk. The ews-rs dependency revision moves from 8806b6d609108a37eeb911753372a4e385159b74 to 1fe0dc6852c1b17820f4e14372bdc1ed008376ee across the local patch configuration, lock and dependency declarations. The19 changed vendored files other than the checksum manifest match its SHA256 entries; this is a static scoped checksum check, not cargo verification or full-crate validation.",
        "ResponseCode moves into the new response module. Each operation response wraps payloads in ResponseClass<T>; the manual visitor selects Success(T), Error(ResponseError) or Warning(T) from the XML attribute. Error data requires MessageText and ResponseCode with optional MessageXml, avoiding success-only fields such as SyncFolderItems Changes on error. Warning keeps T but cannot carry its error fields under the stated XML-library limitation. Unknown or missing response-class attributes return deserialization errors. This is a payload contract, not proof that every server shape or retry case works.",
        "Historical SyncFolderItems clones the current sync token into each request. A typed body ServerBusy sleeps then continues before callbacks, sync-state updates or cursor advancement. Other errors propagate and warnings use their payload. Successful pages call UpdateSyncState, break at IncludesLastItemInRange and otherwise update the next token before OnSyncComplete. The historical single_response_or_error helper rejects zero, warns for multiple and uses the first; it is not exact-one validation. The separate current count helper remains strict.",
        "Historical copy/move response extractors log and skip error messages, then the generic caller can call on_success with the remaining IDs. This is the reviewed staged limitation, not an all-or-nothing success guarantee. Current accepted move_generic instead propagates response_into_messages failure before ID extraction. Do not attribute this later caller behavior or centralized response-processor/token-coordination retry machinery to the initial patch.",
        "Historical distinguished-folder mapping returns a response-class Error before its later ErrorFolderNotFound skip arm, so that later arm cannot catch that earlier typed error. Current accepted source handles optional ErrorFolderNotFound/ErrorSchemaValidation while processing the response class and keeps root errors fatal. This is a source-order difference, not a runtime reproduction, claimed cause of Bug1967333 or inferred tested fix.",
        "Current response_parser recognizes typed body ServerBusy only in the first response message, and separately extracts SOAP Fault delay. The sender consumes Continue, waits on its error-handling token/shared runner and retries the retained request. A typed u32 value is converted to Duration. This does not prove retries for every message in a batch, cancellation behavior, an arbitrary malformed/oversized delay, all copy/move cases or live server operation.",
        "All changed inline parser test hunks in copy_item, create_item, move_folder, move_item, soap and update_folder were read. The new body-busy fixture directly checks Error data with BackOffMilliseconds5000 despite absent Changes; the warning fixture directly checks a synthetic usable payload and explicitly states its limitation. Neither directly asserts waiting, retry count, cursor retention or callback order. Historical new assert_eq! calls at soap.rs486/625 omit assertion messages; the nearby expect text is not the assertion message. Current SOAP helper216 and test_utils31/41 also omit equality-assertion messages. These scoped omissions are recorded under the deliberate assertion rule; no imported-code rewrite or automatic policy change is made.",
        "Imported CI adds warning-denying Rust flags, workspace tests, test-aware clippy and private-item docs checks. README/link/license and checksum changes are scoped metadata. No CI job, cargo test, clippy, docs build, Thunderbird test, native server, build or runtime ran. Rust match/early-return/error propagation and concise limitation comments are studied in their own scope; no JavaScript style rule is exported to this crate.",
        "Bug1971330: full available description, comments0–3, updates and footer read from the retained canonical capture. The supplied SOAP example puts ErrorServerBusy and BackOffMilliseconds5000 inside a SyncFolderItems response message, omits Changes and therefore previously failed the success-payload deserializer. Comment1 speculates about another folder-sync bug; no source/runtime proof establishes that relationship. Subsequent attachment/landing updates are historical process evidence, not a live-server test.",
        "D258019: complete retained timeline and current summary read; no submitted inline bodies or summary-edit histories exist in the capture. Concern: existing whole-operation copy/move assumptions cannot robustly retry per-item errors. Author response/change: land response-class parsing and observed body-backoff handling, log/skip per-item errors for the current API, then address wider copy/move retry handling separately. Reviewer accepts that staged scope and requests a separate issue; the author records Bug1978577. Review acceptance and landing do not establish all retry cases or all-or-nothing copy/move behavior.",
        "Outcome is source-scoped: the historical diff adds generic response/error parsing and SyncFolderItems body-backoff retry while preserving the stated follow-up limit. Accepted code is a later phase with a first-message backoff processor, shared retry waiting and error-propagating copy/move caller. Historical basic-testing/Try reports remain private reports; no linked job, external ews-rs PR, SOAP reference, unrelated CalDAV landing parent or related bug body was opened or inferred.",

Warning comments explain a real serialization-library limit, and cursor/backoff observations name when state remains valid. The assertion-message omissions are reported at exact selected source lines; no vendor or local source changes, rule edits, tests or runtime were performed."
